clue.text: Biblical character to tease about epistle

indicators.note: about means the word for teasing goes around the letter

parts.note: to josh is to tease or kid
EP is the standard abbreviation for epistle

explanation.surface: A Bible figure is ribbed about a letter he wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph, son of Jacob with the coat of many colours, is a figure from the Old Testament.

clue.text: Joust's getting toppled in a precise way

indicators.note: toppled says the letters are knocked over and set up in a new order

parts.note: the word with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A knight's tilt is upset, and done exactly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toppled' rearranges the six letters of JOUSTS; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Just so is an idiom for exactly right, arranged precisely as it should be.

clue.text: Uncle Rod's devious villain

indicators.note: devious, meaning crooked, signals the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A relative called Rod turns out to be a crafty rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoundrel is a dishonest rogue, a synonym for a villain.

clue.text: Saw pirate in lead

indicators.note: in places the seafarer inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: PB is the chemical symbol for lead
a rover is an old word for a pirate

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is seen in a lead mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying, the same thing as a proverb.

clue.text: Reliant three-wheeler initially showing signs of corrosion

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the vehicle word

parts.note: a car showing corrosion is rusting

explanation.surface: An old Reliant three-wheeled car is starting to rust.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reliant Robin was a British three-wheeled car, so 'Reliant' poses as a brand name; here it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reliant on others is dependent on them, trusting in their support.

clue.text: Prehistoric dwellings with article missing from circuitous route

indicators.note: missing from says a piece is removed from the longer phrase

parts.note: going round the houses is the idiom for taking a roundabout route
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Ancient huts are reached by a winding path lacking a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundhouses were the circular huts of the British Iron and Bronze Ages, a prehistoric home.

clue.text: Show relief before troublesome youth once is seen

indicators.note: before puts the breath of relief ahead of the youth

parts.note: to sigh is to show relief by breathing out
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a rowdy 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: A sigh of relief goes up when an old tearaway is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighted means spotted or seen, past participle of the verb to sight.

clue.text: Ball collected by football team up in Scottish ground

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the whole thing is read from bottom to top
collected by means the sphere is held inside the eleven

parts.note: XI, Roman eleven, is a football side
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A football squad gathers the ball at a Scottish stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole assembly over, XORBI becoming the answer. IBROX is the home ground of Rangers in Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibrox Stadium in Glasgow is a famous Scottish football ground, home to Rangers.

clue.text: One can't see vessel near centre of storm

parts.note: a glass is a drinking vessel
the eye is the calm centre of a hurricane

explanation.surface: A ship sails near the heart of a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificial eye made of glass gives no vision, so it is something that cannot see.

clue.text: Perfect time to enter club

indicators.note: to enter places the time letter inside the golf club

parts.note: a spoon is an old name for a golf club

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to walk into a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a nightclub; a spoon was an old lofted wooden golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot-on is a British idiom for exactly right, perfect.

clue.text: Secretly record song about liberal country

indicators.note: about says the bugging and song go around the party letter

parts.note: to bug is to record secretly with a hidden microphone
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Someone covertly tapes a song about a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulgaria is a country in south-east Europe.

clue.text: Despatched criminal leader in need to reform

definitions.text: Despatched criminal leader in need to reform

parts.note: despatched means sent off

indicators.note: in places the head letter inside the reworked word
to reform means the letters are formed again in a new order
leader picks out the opening letter of the wrongdoer word

explanation.surface: A gang boss is sent down because he needs to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' gives ENED, and 'in' puts C inside it. Read whole, the clue also describes a convict sent down.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal despatched to prison by a judge, needing reform, has been sentenced.

clue.text: Rugby player getting tired out in track through London

indicators.note: in places the exhausted phrase inside the rugby position

parts.note: a centre is a back position in rugby
all in is an idiom for exhausted

explanation.surface: An exhausted rugby back heads through the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central Line is a London Underground line running east to west across the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central Line is a Tube route, a railway track running through London.

clue.text: State of silent exasperation

indicators.note: of says the answer is made out of letters within the phrase

explanation.surface: A condition of quiet irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like 'condition' but is a US state, found inside silenT EXASperation.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Outlaw's horse in northern resort

parts.note: Robin Hood is the outlaw of English legend
a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.surface: A legendary outlaw's steed is found at a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood's Bay is a fishing village and resort on the North Yorkshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood's Bay is a coastal resort in North Yorkshire, in the north of England.

clue.text: Expensive bit of bling I obtain with restricted credit

indicators.note: bit of picks out the opening letter of the jewellery word
restricted means the obtaining verb hems in the credit word

parts.note: to get is to obtain
tick is British slang for credit

explanation.surface: A bit of flashy jewellery is pricey when buying on a limited loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A big-ticket item is a costly one, so the phrase means expensive.

clue.text: David's son taken in by fortune-teller

indicators.note: taken in by means the son letter is held inside the palm reader

parts.note: a palmist tells fortunes by reading palms

explanation.surface: David's boy is duped by a clairvoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'David's son' suggests Solomon; the 's is 'is', and King David is traditionally the author of the Psalms.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms, so he is known as the psalmist.

clue.text: Little Sarah given talking to for sauce

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah
addressing someone is talking to them

explanation.surface: Young Sarah gets a telling-off for being cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' poses as cheek, as in a scolding, but is a salad topping.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad dressing is a sauce poured over a salad.

clue.text: Cooked bird somewhere in Ireland

parts.note: food cooked through is done
bird is slang for a girl, as is gal

explanation.surface: A roasted fowl served somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' suggests poultry beside 'Cooked', but is slang for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a county in the north-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Butt in after one no-trump lacking manners

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
NT is the bridge abbreviation for no-trump
rude means lacking manners

explanation.surface: A bridge player rudely interrupts after a bid of one no-trump.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to interrupt or intrude on others.

clue.text: Spies a toilet

parts.note: the Gents is a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: Secret agents use a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents is a plural synonym for spies, as in secret agents.

clue.text: French newspaper's disregarding of French a complete failure

indicators.note: disregarding means the French word for of is left out

parts.note: Le Monde is a leading French newspaper
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A Paris daily ignores French affairs and is a total flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is slang for a dud, something that is a total failure.

clue.text: Measuring device agreed with every reading initially

parts.note: met as in met with approval, agreed with

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letters of the last two words

explanation.surface: An instrument matched every measurement at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter is an instrument for measuring something like gas or electricity.

clue.text: Punishment includes not drinking alcohol before going to bed

indicators.note: includes means the punishment word holds the teetotal letters

parts.note: a lashing is a whipping, a punishment
TT stands for teetotal

explanation.surface: A whipping is given to someone sober before bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Last thing is an idiom for at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Last thing means at the end of the day, just before retiring for the night.

clue.text: Toiling arduously about a method of printing

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters surround the single letter
arduously suggests struggling effort, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Labouring hard over a printing technique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arduously' rearranges TOILING, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Intaglio is an engraving technique where the image is cut into the plate, used for printing.

clue.text: Bright light gets former mayor depressed

parts.note: the sun is a bright light
Ken Livingstone was a former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Strong sunshine leaves a former mayor feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressed' looks like gloomy but means pressed down, set low.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken means lying below the surrounding level, pressed down or hollow.

clue.text: Singer putting heart in popular album

indicators.note: putting in says the card letter is placed inside the singer word
putting in says the card letter is placed inside the singer word

parts.note: a triller is one who trills, a singer
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A singer puts emotion into a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Jackson's Thriller is the best-selling album of all time.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriller by Michael Jackson is one of the most popular albums ever released.

clue.text: River systems approaching the sea could become salted

indicators.note: could become means the letters may change into something new

explanation.surface: Rivers nearing the ocean might turn salty.
explanation.definitionFit: Deltas are the fan-shaped systems of channels a river forms near the sea.
